convoLines.text: "They'd tell me to keep working. So I'm working. That's the whole plan."
Ava has an edge today — something curdled.
"Most days I don't think about it. Today I am. Appreciate you noticing."
"Marta owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"I keep turning over the last thing Marta said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"We bury, we grieve, we keep going. There's no step four."
"Still on what's been happening. Seen worse."
You show them Elderberry — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Thanks for... you know. Just listening."
"This was good." They mean it.
"It's quiet today. Wrong kind of quiet."
"Heh. Nobody's asked me that in a while. ...I'm alright. Getting there."
"I dreamed Marta was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
"Another time. The village needs me here."
"Sleep's gone strange. I count portions out loud before eating at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
You show them Elderberry — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"I should go before I say something sincere."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"We gave them a good burial. Doesn't feel like enough, does it?"
Giuseppe has an edge today — something curdled.
A long exhale. "I'll get there. Just needed a minute where I didn't have to be fine."
"Marta always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
You show them Yarrow — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"They're already drifting away. "Later."
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
Ava: "I've heard good things about Emberhold. We should link with them — we'd be stronger together."
"Walk with me? I want another pair of eyes on something."
"All right — let's ask them." You carry the proposal to Emberhold.
"What got you through the first week? The very first days."
"Between us — Shock's underrated. It's the body's way of buying you time."
"Can I be honest? Spite, mostly. Pure, clean spite at the sky. Then someone shared food with me and the spite turned into something else. I still don't have a word for the something else."
"Still on what got you through the first week."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Good question." "Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "Since Marta died... I keep expecting to see Marta at the fire. Stupid."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Ava grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Ava is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"About the pantry run — I hate to ask twice, but it's still open. Will you?"
"Another day like today and we're choosing who eats. I know the staghorn sumac patch past the treeline — come with me and we'll fill packs before dark."
Move next to your partner, on the same side of the Haven door.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Last time things were different. They always are." "Marta is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"I count portions out loud before eating for Marta, now. Feels right. Feels like the least I can do."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Ava nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Well. My social battery is officially dead."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"Good — what's been happening, settled. Feels better said out loud."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Can I trust you? I mean really."
"That's the right answer. The wrong one would've been 'yes' too fast."
"Can I be honest? I'll tell you what I tell everyone: watch what I do when nobody's watching. That's the whole of me. The rest is just talking."
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Still on whether they can trust you…"
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Xenia nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
A flicker at the corner of their mouth. Not quite a smile. Not quite anything.
"Fine." Sharp. "You want to hear it? I dug it up. I was starving and your hole was right there. Happy now?"
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"I've decided to treat this as an extended camping trip. A terrible, endless camping trip."
"Come get air with me. I need to think out loud."
Xenia shows you where they go to think. "Don't tell the others. Everyone needs one place."
"I still need help with the pantry run."
As I said — Move next to your partner, on the same side of the Haven door.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Shannon nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"We were just talking. Nothing important."
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"Good question." "You're family now. Chosen family — the kind that actually counts." "Make of that what you will."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."

"We never did finish talking about grief — that was 11 days back. Still on your mind? 'A long exhale. I'll get there. Just needed a minute where I didn't have to be fine.' We still owe what's been happening a proper ending, too."
"Come see what I found. You won't believe it."
It's quiet at the hollow. Giuseppe doesn't say much. Sometimes that's the whole point.
"Thanks. ...Thanks for saying that."
"You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "You want to know what I did in the raid? I put down Nostalgia at the treeline. Don't call it brave. Call it awake."
"I can't. Not today. Ask me when the work's done."
You show them Lamb's Quarters — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"...I need to go be quiet for a while."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
You said you'd earn it, not that I should just hand it over. Fair. I'm watching — and so far, so good.
"Walk with me? I want another pair of eyes on something."
Shannon shows you where they go to think. "Don't tell the others. Everyone needs one place."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on that personal stuff."
"Yeah? What's up?"
"Good question." "They say the table's coming. For us. I keep thinking about what we'd even bring to it."
"Seven doors and it chose US. I retie every loose knot in passing and try to feel chosen instead of chosen-at."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"I should get back to it."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Can I tell you something? Before the scattering, I stole from someone who trusted me. I think about it every day."
Milo has an edge today — something curdled.
"Thank you. ...I needed someone to know, and I needed it to stop there. Thank you. Really."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"I wish there was more to tell. That's it."
"Sure — what's on your mind? It'll be fun, probably."
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Have you felt it? Like the air before a storm, but — bigger. Something's on its way."
"All right. Thank you for telling me."
"Anyway — I should get going."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.

lines: d21: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Marta Vega is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d21: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d21: 🕯️ Marta Vega is dead — the night. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d21: What Marta kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d21: "Marta's gone." Ava looks at you for a long moment. "You're not Marta." No heat in it. Just fact. You'll have to earn this face.
d21: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Ines blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.
d21: 📖 LEARNED: Herbal Medicine (Level 1). Willow bark = aspirin. Yarrow stops bleeding. Plantain draws out infection. The pharmacy is outside.
d21: 📖 LEARNED: Reading the Land (Level 1). Eat the landscape with your eyes first: green + water + sun means food grows here. Start where those three meet.
d21: 📖 LEARNED: The Forager’s Eye (Level 1). You walk slower and see more. Food was always there; now you notice it.
d21: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d21: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Marta Vega, 21 days. The mantle passes to Ines Duarte.
d21: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Ines Duarte, 33 — a florist. Her hands know different work now: The Touch.
d21: The village's quarrel was with Marta — and Marta is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d21: At the grave, Tomás, Ava speak for Ines — "Marta trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
d21: The fire knew Ines before the Codex did — her name already carried weight here.

lastSay: d51: 🍽️ Xenia sets the sharing basket down by the fire instead of the pantry. "Full shelves don't need my little more."
d52: — DAY 52 DAWN — The world wakes. Animals are active.
d52: 💬 Grace says: "Dreamed again. They showed me teeth. Lots of teeth. Be ready to fight soon."
d52: Word with the traders: Emberhold door is clear again. Whatever had them, let go.
d52: Dawn. You wake rested. (+0 health, energy restored. Your sleeping body burned less — 89 kcal conserved. By the fire. Good enough.)
